primary_meaning: Purity, chastity, and undivided devotion/fidelity to God (most prominently embodied by Mary in the virgin birth of Christ, and secondarily by the Church or faithful as Christ's pure bride)
primary_basis: Matthew 1:18-25 and Luke 1:26-38 (Mary's virginal conception by the Holy Spirit)
2 Corinthians 11:2 (Church presented as pure virgin to Christ)
Matthew 25:1-13 (parable of the wise and foolish virgins)
Revelation 14:4 (the 144,000 as virgins who follow the Lamb)

alternatives.meaning: Personification of Israel/Zion/Judah as the 'virgin daughter' (vulnerable yet elect people of God)
Literal lifelong sexual abstinence as a higher spiritual calling or state of perfection (especially in Catholic/Orthodox monastic and Marian teaching on perpetual virginity)
basis: traditional interpretation of Luke 1:34 and John 19:26-27

alternatives.meaning: Moral/spiritual innocence free from idolatry or worldliness (without necessarily implying sexual status)

notes: Across patristic, medieval, Reformation, and modern biblical scholarship and teaching, 'virgin' consistently functions as a symbol of purity and exclusive belonging to God. The Marian application is the single most dominant Christian usage; the corporate (Israel/Church) and individual purity applications are also standard and non-conflicting. No major tradition treats the term as lacking symbolic content.
